## Natural history notes

A small snout moth characterized by pale tan to straw-colored wings with fine darker speckling, faint lines, and a narrow triangular resting posture. In Florida, the Paler Moodna Moth is likely found in warm open or semi-open habitats such as pine flatwoods, fields, roadsides, gardens, marsh edges, and weedy areas where adults may come to lights. Its caterpillar host plants appear poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small nocturnal plant-feeding moth whose larvae likely feed concealed on low vegetation or plant debris, while adults and larvae support birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
